description:
Scope: planning only for lib/zaq/channels/mattermost_admin.ex lines 67, 72, 76, 113, 159, 204. Exclusive test path to EDIT: test/zaq/channels/mattermost_admin_test.exs. No production, other test/support, docs, or Git changes; no test execution now. Existing test/zaq/channels/mattermost_membership_test.exs already covers injected pagination, limits, invalid page and deduplication; preserve it, do not duplicate. Existing shared-history integration tests cover cross-room rejection. MattermostAdmin @moduledoc owns BO admin browse/send/management, not ingress. Action reuse: not applicable—test-only coverage, no changed executable operation, Action, agent tool, workflow or execution boundary. No new UI journey/E2E or documentation update.

Test-first scenarios and missed-line map (call public functions; assert exact observable results):
1. Line 67: fetch_room_message(%{url: "https://example.invalid", token: "test-token"}, valid_26_char_room, nil) returns {:error, :unavailable}. Non-binary message_id selects fallback without an HTTP request; also optionally use integer ID. Distinguish this from an invalid binary ID, which enters guarded clause then its else. No network call for this case.
2. Line 72: locally serve a root post via existing OpenAIStub.server/2; GET /v1/api/v4/posts/root-1 responds 200 with exact id "root-1", channel_id matching requested room, root_id "", user_id "human-1", message "root", and create_at an integer far outside DateTime millisecond range (e.g. 10 ** 30; verify DateTime.from_unix/2 returns {:error, _} on this value before locking the fixture). Call fetch_room_message/3 with stub URL and config.settings %{ "jido_chat" => %{ "bot_user_id" => "bot-1"}}. Assert {:ok, %{author_id: "human-1", content: "root", role: "external", inserted_at: nil, attachments: []}}; assert observed GET path. This exercises integer timestamp parse failure rather than noninteger fallback.
3. Line 76: same root-post stub with create_at omitted or a binary "not-a-millisecond"; assert identical root fields and inserted_at: nil. Use a second request/stub instance or a parameterized local fixture function only if repetition warrants it. Keep line 72 and 76 independently observable; optionally include a valid millisecond case to assert a known UTC DateTime and guard against always-nil mapping.
4. Line 113: add explicit fetch_bot_user_id/2 tests with existing local HTTP stub: valid /users/me id+username yields {:ok, "bot-user-1"}; malformed identity yields {:error, :invalid_identity}, and/or HTTP 401 yields {:error, "HTTP 401"}. Assert the observed GET /v1/api/v4/users/me and that the wrapper preserves errors, not merely a shape. fetch_bot_identity/2 already covers each response class.
5. Line 159: channel_membership_snapshot(%{}, valid_26_char_room, %{fetch_page: fn ... end}) returns {:error, :invalid_channel_id}; separately nil channel ID with [] opts. A map opts fails the is_list guard; do not pass malformed fetch_page inside a keyword list because that would invoke the callback and raise. room_members(%{}, nil) may be asserted to propagate this error too.
6. Line 204: call channel_membership_snapshot(%{url: stub_url, token: "test-token"}, valid_26_char_room) WITHOUT fetch_page injection; the default fetch_membership_page/4 must issue GET /v1/api/v4/channels/<room>/members with query page=0 and per_page=200. Stub returns 200 [%{"user_id" => "member-1"}]; assert {:ok, %{complete: true, member_ids: ["member-1"]}} and observed request path/query (and Bearer token where available). Optionally exercise room_members/2 with same endpoint to assert identity_platform: "mattermost"; this requires a second HTTP request and is not needed for line 204. Non-200 returns an error, never a partial complete snapshot; existing injected-error test covers propagation.

Fixture/mocks/isolation: reuse current Zaq.DataCase async:false, OpenAIStub.server/2 and start_supervised!/1. Use the local stub instead of real Mattermost/network; no new Mox or app-env mutation. DB fixture insert_mattermost_config/1 is NOT needed for direct root, identity or membership APIs; retain it only for existing send/clear tests. Use unique test-local ports from OpenAIStub, explicit request observations, no sleeps/polling; assert responses after synchronous calls. Existing async:false remains because this file contains DB-backed config/global interaction; do not change isolation as part of coverage. No new support helper unless repetition merits a private local root-post builder. Property assessment: current membership property already covers deduplication over broad inputs; these are finite guard, wrapper and timestamp-boundary cases better proven by concrete examples, so no new property. If timestamp magnitude boundary becomes an invariant over broad values, consider bounded StreamData alongside these examples, not instead of them.

Blockers/unreachable: no confirmed unreachable line; line 72 depends on DateTime.from_unix(huge_integer, :millisecond) returning {:error, _} rather than raising or succeeding; check against installed Elixir version during later implementation and record a real blocker if no integer can yield an error. line 204 requires no injected fetch_page; injection bypasses it. If OpenAIStub callback cannot expose query/header, assert its observed request message or inspect test support contract; do not silently omit endpoint verification or add production test hooks.

Later validation only: run isolated mix test test/zaq/channels/mattermost_admin_test.exs and existing mattermost_membership_test.exs through Context Mode, then mix q; inspect diff and preserve existing assertions. After implementation and review approval generate fresh mix coveralls.json with 600000ms timeout, then mix coverup only on success, verify all six exact lines and meaningful branch outcomes; record unavoidable exceptions in Beadwork/PR. Follow final mix precommit 900000ms gate before requesting final human approval. No tests/coverage/Git actions during this planning task. One independent Channels test surface; no dependencies.
